newsitem.title: CHINA: China vows to get tougher with bicycle theft.
newsitem.headline: China vows to get tougher with bicycle theft.

text.p: Chinese police have vowed to slap tougher penalties on bicycle thieves after the number of such thefts shot up eight times last year, a police official said on Wednesday.

The Ministry of Public Security was expected to introduce in two months a new set of regulations that would include both criminal and administrative penalties for bicycle theft, a ministry official said by telephone.
Currently, bicycle thieves receive only warnings or fines because of the difficulty in gathering evidence in such cases.
About 80,000 bicycles were reported missing last year compared with 10,000 the year earlier, the China Daily newspaper said.
Under the rules, new apartment buildings would be required to build bicycle parking lots in future and bicycle manufacturers would be encouraged to build locks into handlebars, the official said.
Bicycle ownership information would be kept on computer along with household registration using the census management system, the China Daily said.
Bicycles are the main means of transportation in China, the world's most populous nation with 1.2 billion people.
